title: Russell US Style indexes — conditional quarter-end recapping takes effect at the open, on the same session as the S&P Select Sector breach test (24% / 4.8% thresholds on both)
source: EST: owner-published, read direct this session. FTSE Russell, "Frequently Asked Questions -- Russell US Equity Indexes", July 2026 (lseg.com dam policy-documents PDF, ftse-faq-document-russell-us-equity-2026.pdf, HTTP 200, 198,134 bytes, 19 content streams inflated and text-extracted in-session 2026-09-06). THE DATE: the same dated four-column schedule table this calendar's russell-quarterly-ipo-review-effective-2026-09-21 entry cites carries two further rows, quoted verbatim -- "Russell US Style Quarter-end Capping Cut-Off Date | 26 March 2026 | 25 June 2026 | 25 SEPTEMBER 2026 | 28 December 2026" and "Russell US Style Quarter-end Capping Effective Date (open of, if applicable) | 31 March 2026 | 30 June 2026 | 30 SEPTEMBER 2026 | 31 December 2026". THE RULE, in the same document's "Regulatory Capping" section and also verbatim: "applicable capped Russell US Style Indexes are subject to a quarter-end capping check to ensure constituent weights remain within defined thresholds. The review is conducted quarterly (March, June, September, and December) using closing prices from three trading days prior to the last business day of the quarter", testing "whether ... capped weight exceeds 24%, or whether companies with weights above 4.8% collectively exceed 48% of the index", and "Where a breach is identified, the index is recapped in accordance with the applicable capping methodology, with the updated weights becoming effective on the last business day of the quarter. If no breach is identified, no changes are made." The published cut-off (25 September 2026) and effective date (30 September 2026) both reproduce that rule against the 2026 calendar, which is the internal check. THE EVENT IS CONDITIONAL BY CONSTRUCTION and is labelled so: it fires only on a breach, exactly like the sp-select-sector-secondary-reweight-2026-09-30 entry this calendar already carries. Filed estimate because this lane may not flip a status without an IR:/BLS:/FED: primary, the confirmed-tier prefixes have no member for an index owner's own published schedule, and the FAQ table carries the owner's caveat "NOTE: Dates may be subject to change. Clients will be notified of any changes." Discovered during the russell-quarterly-ipo-review-effective-2026-09-21 initial research, checked 2026-09-06
notes: PROPOSED by the russell-quarterly-ipo-review-effective-2026-09-21 initial research (2026-09-06), which found it while reading the owner's own schedule table for the quarterly IPO effective date -- two rows below it in the same column. WHY IT IS WORTH A CALENDAR ENTRY, and it is not the size of the flow: this calendar ALREADY tracks sp-select-sector-secondary-reweight-2026-09-30, S&P's conditional quarter-end concentration test, on the identical date. The two index families run near-identical conditional recaps into the SAME OPEN with near-identical triggers -- Russell tests a 24% single-name cap and whether names above 4.8% collectively exceed 48%; the S&P Select Sector secondary reweight tests 24% / 4.8% / 50%. Because both tests key off the same handful of mega-cap weights measured over the same quarter, they are strongly correlated: they will tend to fire together or not at all, and if they fire, two families' worth of recapping flow lands on one session. That correlation is the finding, and it is an execution-hygiene fact rather than a directional claim. SCOPE IS SMALL AND IS STATED UP FRONT: the owner says plainly that this framework "applies to applicable capped Russell US Style Indexes and does not apply to the capitalisation-weighted Russell 1000 or Russell 2000 Indexes" -- so IWM and the broad Russell trackers are untouched, and nothing here reaches the names this house watches unless it holds a capped style product. Impact low and symbols deliberately EMPTY for the same reasons as every Russell sibling: the flow is in individual constituent weights, an ETF proxy would make the deterministic screen trip on beta, and no house playbook is index-flow-keyed. Kind sector matches both the Russell siblings and the S&P entry it pairs with. THE PROPOSING RESEARCH'S OWN VERDICT TRAVELS WITH THIS PROPOSAL so nobody sizes it as tradable: that research measured the quarterly Russell leg and found no index-level effect in the only instrument this house has, and it separately measured that instrument to be near-blind to Russell flow generally -- even the JUNE RECONSTITUTION implementation Friday, the largest index-flow day of the year, prints IWM relative turnover of only 1.13x mean / 1.06x median at 12 of 21 above 1.0, against an all-session baseline of 1.03x / 0.99x. A conditional capping event confined to style indexes is smaller again. This entry earns its place as awareness of what is on the tape and as the pair to the S&P entry, not as a trade.
